bodyHtml:
Thinking of gifting property to your loved ones? To give a child a little something extra, or to thank your parent for their time and love, giving a property to loved ones through a Gift Deed is the most endearing way to show love and care.

But, before you get started embodying that love, it is essential to know the stamp duty on a gift deed, a critical step that legitimizes your intention to gift the property and renders your act legally valid and binding.

In India, a Gift Deed is not only a procedural necessity. It is a legal document recognized under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. Furthermore, the correct stamp duty on the gift will be paid, so your rights of ownership remain protected.

What is a Gift Deed?

A Gift Deed is a legal document that enables the voluntary transfer of property ownership without receiving any compensation in return. It allows you to gift your property to someone else - typically a family member - such as your spouse, parents, or children.

Unlike a Sale Deed, where money changes hands, a Gift Deed is a no-consideration transfer. A Gift Deed is also different from a Will, which only takes effect when the person writing the Will passes away, whereas a Gift Deed is valid immediately upon execution and registration.

To effectuate the transfer, you must register the Gift Deed at the sub-registrar's office and pay the requisite gift deed registration fees and stamp duty on the gift deed.

Why Stamp Duty is Important for Gift Deeds

Think of stamp duty as a fee charged by the government to confirm the transfer of your ownership in the eyes of the law. Without paying stamp duty, your deed of gift stamp duty document carries no legal authority at all.

Stamp duty also:

  • Verifies the authenticity of the property transfer and
  • Documents your rightful ownership of the property
  • Protects the giver and the receiver from any potential disputes in the future

What is interesting is that gifting property and stamp duty rules vary by state and to whom you give the property.

Stamp Duty Rates on Gift Deeds Across Indian States

Here’s a quick look at how the gift of property stamp duty differs across major Indian states. Notice how blood relation gifts often enjoy big concessions!

State Gift to Family Members Gift to Non-Family Members Registration Charges
Tamil Nadu 1% of market value 7% of market value 1%
Maharashtra ₹200 (fixed) 3% of market value 1%
Delhi Nil (for blood relations) 3% 1%
Karnataka ₹1,000 (family) 5% 1%

Pro Tip: In some states, female recipients enjoy lower property gift deed charges as part of women's empowerment schemes.

Note: - The percentage might vary due to different reasons, so please check the official website of the respective state.

Exemptions and Concessions

Good news, you may not always be subject to the full stamp duty on a gift deed in blood relation cases!

The extent of the exemption typically depends on a state permitting partial or complete exemption when transferring the property to a parent, spouse, child, or sibling. For example:

  • Maharashtra — Flat ₹200 duty for transferring to a family member.
  • Tamil Nadu — Only 2% stamp duty for transfer to a close relative.

This will not only allow you to utilize reasonable transfer rates, but it will also make this gifting process simpler.

Step-by-Step Process to Register a Gift Deed in India

Here’s what the gift deed registration process looks like:

  • Prepare a clear Gift Deed with all donor and donee information.
  • Pay the gift deed stamp paper value and registration charges for the gift deed.
  • Submit all documents to the nearest Sub-Registrar Office.
  • Both donor and donee, and any witness, must be physically present for biometric verification.
  • Collect the registered document after it is completed.

List of Documents Needed for a Gift Deed in India

  • ID proof of donor & donee
  • Original property documents
  • Relationship proof (for exemption)
  • Recent property tax receipts

Tip: Don’t delay registration — incomplete or unregistered deeds are invalid in court.

How Gifted Property Is Taxed in India

Tax is another crucial factor in understanding gift deed stamp duty.

Per Section 56 (2) of the Income Tax Act, if the gifted property is to a relative, there is no tax due. If gifted as a “non-relative” and the value of the property is greater than ₹50,000, then it is taxable in the classification of “Income from Other Sources.”

If the receiver later sells the property, capital gains tax will apply, calculated from the original owner’s purchase cost.

Common Errors to Avoid While Preparing a Gift Deed

  • Disregarding the necessity for stamp paper for a gift deed.
  • Believing every family gift is exempt from tax (not necessarily the case).
  • Not registering to "save costs" -- it may end up costing more down the road.
  • Forgetting to consider the gift deed stamp duty calculator to calculate the amount you will owe accurately.

Expert Advice for Property Owners Planning to Execute a Gift Deed

  • Before completing the deed, always check for state-specific guidelines.
  • Seek clarity on legal matters from a reputable property counsel.
  • Retain records of all receipts, documentation, and authorizations.
  • If you intend to buy property in Chennai, being aware of local gift deed charges will help avoid being caught off guard later.

In Conclusion, A Gift Deed is not just a legal document; it is a token of trust and love. That said, for your gift deed to be legally enforceable, you must pay the requisite stamp duty on the gift deed and register it correctly.

If you are aware of all the gift deed registration charges or any exemptions, completing the property transfer will be easier, cheaper, and less argumentative.
